audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagreed with their own why-text. The chart read Skill/Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Skill/Skill/Tryndamere/Tryndamere while whys[0] says to concede level 1, whys[1] calls level 2 'your first real edge', whys[2] calls level 3 'your hardest swing', whys[3] says you out-trade him, and whys[5] and whys[6] both say the late game is even rather than his.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Tryndamere/Jax/Jax/Jax/Skill/Skill/Skill at 51.17% over 1284 games — his level 1, your 2 through 5, then a genuine wash once Undying Rage exists. The prose already told that story.
audit.corrected: Rows set to Tryndamere / Jax / Jax / Jax / Skill / Skill / Skill in both layers, ratings realigned to 3, 7, 7, 7, 5, 5, 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage was described only as 'Unkillable 5s' with no cooldown, so 'commit on its cooldown' gave the reader nothing to count.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80s. At rank 1 that is longer than your own ultimate (110s), so early on you genuinely can fight on its cooldown; by rank 3 it is 80s and comes back faster than yours, which is why the late rows flatten to Skill.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[4].why carry the 120s figure.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is described everywhere as a 'back-turned slow' without ever telling the reader what to do about it, and no cooldowns were given for it or for Spinning Slash.
audit.why: Riot's Mocking Shout text: it reduces surrounding champions' Attack Damage, and enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced — 14s flat, 850 range. So the slow is conditional on you running away: walking toward him or laterally takes the AD reduction only. That is a concrete, actionable interaction the page never stated. Spinning Slash is 12/11/10/9/8s at 650 range, the dash you want spent before you commit. Counter Strike dodges attacks, so it does blank his crit autos — the page has that right.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now states the back-turned condition as an instruction; breakdown.cooldowns carries Mocking Shout's 14s alongside Undying Rage.
sources: brief enemyKit W text and cd 14

audit.whatIsWrong: Only Undying Rage was tracked, and without a number.
audit.why: Spinning Slash at 12s rank 1 is the cooldown that decides whether he can kite your stun, and Mocking Shout at 14s is the one that decides whether he can run you down — both matter more moment to moment than his ultimate.

edits.before: Auto-trade only with E held in your pocket. Identify how Tryndamere contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: No Counter Strike yet, so his crit autos go unpunished and Fury-fed Bloodlust heals your poke back — concede and farm.

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Tryndamere's Undying Rage is down.
edits.after: Empower gives a front-loaded burst his single-target spin cannot match yet — your first real edge in the lane.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Tryndamere must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Counter Strike online: the dodge blanks his crit autos and the recast stun punishes a committed Spinning Slash.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Undying Rage's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Counter Strike (11s at rank 4) refreshes faster than he lands a full auto string, so you out-trade while your on-hits ramp.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Tryndamere's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Your R makes the all-in look lethal, but Undying Rage (120s at rank 1) holds him at 1 HP for 5s — bait it or you waste the combo.

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Undying Rage's cooldown.
edits.after: Trinity trades evenly with his first crit item and lifesteal — a duel you win but can't finish.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Tryndamere carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: You out-DPS him at two items, but Undying Rage, Bloodlust and his spin kite mean you cannot close it — trade towers instead.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then trade. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 120s at rank 1 and 5s of unkillable — bait it or wait it out, then trade.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then trade. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: 120/100/80s — 5s unkillable, so wait it out and trade after. - Mocking Shout: 14s, and it only slows you with your back turned — never flee in a straight line. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then trade. When it is down — Q-E-W him.
edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows you with your back turned — walk toward him or sideways, never straight away.

notes: Left in place, unverified: the page says in whys[2], spikes[1], early, mid and wants.you[0] that the Counter Strike recast stun 'interrupts his Spinning Slash' mid-dash. Riot's Spinning Slash text carries no channel or interruptible language and the kit has no matching flag, so I could not confirm the interrupt and did not edit those lines. suspectNames entries ('Mocking Shout's', 'Bank Fury', 'Pop Undying Rage') are all false positives — the names are correct. Packet games (1284) disagrees with the brief's top-level games (2925). Content layer says 'Grandmaster at Arms' for Jax's R while the full layer says 'Grandmaster's Might'; per the teemo mirror, Data Dragon 16.15.1 calls it 'Grandmaster-at-Arms', so the full layer's name is the stale one.
